changelog: - **`Organization.vertical` — the foundation for coreCRM's verticals** (#2350, epic #2348). The app is becoming one core serving several products (internship CRM today, a marketing CRM next), and which product a tenant sees is now a property of the *tenant*, not of the deployment: a `vertical` column on `Organization` (literal default `INTERNSHIP`, so `db push` fills existing rows itself), a frozen catalogue in `src/lib/verticals.ts` declaring each vertical's capabilities, and `verticalFor(orgId)` / `verticalsFor(ids)` in `src/lib/verticalContext.ts`. The read ALWAYS takes an explicit `orgId` and is never put in the JWT — `role` is in the token and the schema's own SUPER_ADMIN note explains what that costs, and most of the surface that will need a vertical later (cron sweeps, newsletter fan-out, webhook dispatch) has no session to read. Super admins can set a vertical when creating a tenant and change it on `/admin/organizations`; a tenant admin cannot change their own, the same rule the plan already carries. Nothing reads the catalogue yet — no capability is gated, no label changes, no route moves — so this ships with zero behaviour change by construction, and a unit test pins the ways that could stop being true: an unknown key must fall back to `INTERNSHIP` rather than to an empty capability set, and `INTERNSHIP` must remain a superset of every capability any vertical declares. The per-vertical stage preset is deliberately NOT in this slice: it would be a plain-string key into `PROGRAM_TEMPLATES` that nothing here resolves, so a wrong key would type-check, pass every test and only surface as an empty pipeline in the slice that finally reads it — it lands in #2353 with the template it points at, a reader, and an e2e.
